newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE confirms big losses at subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: RWE confirms big losses at subsidiary.

text.p: RWE AG, the diversified German energy utility, confirmed on Sunday that a subsidiary had incurred more than 300 million marks ($168.5 million) in operating losses and restructuring costs.

An RWE spokesman said Breuer GmbH, which hires out cranes, made an operating loss of 100 million marks in the business year ended June 30 and had set aside more than 200 million marks to finance a restructuring.

Breuer, which belongs to RWE via its mining subsidiary Rheinbraun AG, had been hit by a slump in the construction industry which had been particularly severe in east Germany, Rheinbraun said in a statement.
The RWE spokesman had on Saturday declined to comment on a magazine report that RWE planned to take a charge of 700 million marks to reflect that some of its subsidiaries were overvalued.
But he said Rheinbraun and a waste management subsidiary, RWE Entsorgung AG, were mulling writing down the value of several firms they had acquired, some in east Germany.
The spokesman declined to specify the extent of the writedowns.
"We are thinking about taking measures in the individual accounts of RWE Entsorgung and Rheinbraun but these will have no impact on the group accounts," RWE spokesman Dieter Schweer said.
Spiegel magazine reported that RWE Entsorgung had paid too much for several of the recycling firms it bought in Germany and eastern Europe over the last seven years.
The market for recycling had been overestimated, Spiegel said in an article released ahead of publication in Monday's editions.
RWE also made no comment on a claim by Spiegel that it wanted Westdeutsche Landesbank (WestLB) to take a stake in RWE to replace local authorities which own about 40 percent.

Spiegel also reported that RWE chief executive Dietmar Kuhnt wanted WestLB to step in as a shareholder to facilitate a restructuring which will see the sale of loss-making units, the replacement of top executives and changes to RWE's accounts.
Some cash-strapped local authorities appeared to be ready to sell their shares, the report said.
Schweer said: "As a rule we don't comment on the activities of our shareholders."
He also described as "speculation" Spiegel's claim that the chief executive of RWE's Otelo telecommunications joint venture with Veba AG, Ulf Bohla, would be replaced in the autumn.
Schweer criticised a study of RWE by Dresdner Kleinwort Benson which said RWE was not well equipped for the liberalisation of the energy market.

The study had "major weaknesses" and had not fully taken into account that the energy division, RWE Energie AG, and Rhienbraun had potential to save a total of 1.5 to two billion marks in the 1997/1998 and 1998/1999 fiscal years.
